#### 5. spermatogenic failure 13  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.383)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-167172, Reactome:R-HSA-73776)

**Proposed mechanism:** ERCC2 (HGNC:3076) —DISRUPTS→ DNA repair (GO:0006281); DNA repair (GO:0006281) —DISRUPTS→ Transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (GO:0006281); Transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (GO:0006281) —LEADS_TO→ DNA damage sensitivity (HP:0002213); Transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (GO:0006281) —LEADS_TO→ Spermatogenic failure (HP:0011328). Loss-of-function mutations in ERCC2 impair its function in DNA repair, particularly in transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair. This disruption leads to increased DNA damage sensitivity, manifesting as xeroderma pigmentosum group D, and also impacts the highly proliferative cells of the testes, leading to spermatogenic failure 13.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ERCC2 with a different functional consequence (e.g., gain-of-function) or variants in completely distinct pathways that do not involve DNA repair for one of the diseases would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if a significant proportion of patients with spermatogenic failure 13 lack ERCC2 mutations and do not present with DNA repair deficiencies, this would also weaken the link. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.001) in ERCC2 associated with both conditions in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ERCC2 in DNA repair and its impact on both somatic cells (leading to cancer predisposition in XP) and germ cells (leading to infertility) could inform therapeutic strategies targeting DNA repair pathways for both cancer and male infertility.
